## Coupled human-natural systems
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 48%;">

**Ecological and social domains are truly one integrated system with complex interactions and feedbacks**

<br/>

**Human survival depends on thriving ecosystems and ecosystem health now depends on the choice humans make**

<br/>

<span style="color:purple;">**In Appalachia, clean headwater streams, intact forests, and stable mountain slopes literally protect towns from floods, landslides, and drinking-water crises**</span>

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:160px; LEFT:550px; WIDTH:450px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/interact.png">

<hr>

## Coupled human-natural systems
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 48%;">

**Ecological and social domains are truly one integrated system with complex interactions and feedbacks**

<br/>

<span style="color:blue">**Successful biodiversity conservation will require addressing needs and inequities in human societies**</span>

<br/>

<span style="color:blue">**Successful social reform and sustainable futures for humans will require biodiversity conservation**</span>

<br/>

<span style="color:red">**Example: Mountaintop-removal mining in Central Appalachia – high global demand for coal, local loss of forest, headwater streams, and community health**</span>

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:160px; LEFT:550px; WIDTH:450px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/mining2.png">

## Coupled human-natural systems
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 52%;">

**Case Study: Are creative solutions possible with mountaintop removal?**

<br/>

**“The fact that coal companies can blast away the tops of 500 of the oldest and most biodiverse mountains on the continent shows an utter disrespect for the communities that have to live with the destruction of their land, air and water,” said Matt Wasson, with Appalachian Voices.**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:160px; LEFT:600px; WIDTH:450px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/miningchart.jpg">


## Coupled human-natural systems
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 52%;">

**Case Study: Are creative solutions possible with mountaintop removal?**

<br/>

<span style="color:blue">**In Appalachia, creative solutions might mean: red spruce restoration, mine-land solar, trail-based economies, floodplain buyouts, and stream restoration instead of more extraction**</span>

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:160px; LEFT:600px; WIDTH:450px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/miningchart.jpg">

## Coupled human-natural systems
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 53%;">

**<span style="color:blue">Creative solutions are possible but they commitment and agreement across individuals – communities – law makers</span>**

<br/>

**The mining industry exploits a federal provision that exempts them from restoring the land to its “approximate original contour” if there is a plan to develop the land for “equal or better economic use” (e.g., industrial, residential or public use)**

<br/>

**However, only ~4% of mountains in Kentucky and West Virginia, where 80 percent of the mining is occurring, have any post-mining economic activity**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:600px; WIDTH:450px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/fail.jpg">

## How can people support biodiversity conservation?
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 48%;">

* **Individuals, as:**
    + consumers
    + funders
    + practitioners
    + activists
    + <span style="color:purple">frequency holders</span>

<br/>

* **Policy actors, through:**
    + fisheries governance
    + endangered species legislation
    + international climate treaties
    + international debt-for-nature swaps

</div>

<div style="float: right; width: 48%;">

* **Collectives, through:**
    + ecotourism
    + sustainable food production
    + community solar projects

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:330px; LEFT:550px; WIDTH:375px; HEIGHT:375px" SRC="images/biod.jpg">

## Root causes: nature's decline
<hr>

<div style="float: left; width: 50%;">
<br/>

* **<span style="color:darkred">What are some of the root causes of biodiversity decline?</span>**
    + Exploitation
    + Capitalism
    + Economic inequality

</div>

<br/>

<div style="float: right; width: 48%;">
 
* **<span style="color:darkred">What are the root causes of these behaviors and social structures?</span>**
    + Greed
    + Fear
    + Complacency
    + Feeling of separation

<br/>

* **<span style="color:darkred">What are the root causes in Appalachia?</span>**
    + coal, gas, timber, and now data-centers
    + ‘resource curse’ economies
    + opioid crisis and health disparities

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:400px; LEFT:0px; WIDTH:580px; HEIGHT:300px" SRC="images/tree.png">

## Root causes affect everything
<hr>
<br/>

**The same extract and deplete mentality is impacting our planet, biosphere, social, emotional, and educational systems…**

<br/>

<span style="color:darkred">**Planet/thermometer: Record-breaking rain events and heat in WV/KY**</span>

<br/>

<span style="color:darkred">**Extinction: “Hemlock woolly adelgid, chestnut blight, red spruce decline, brook trout habitat shrink**</span>

<br/>

<span style="color:darkred">**Hunger/poverty: “Food deserts and energy poverty in rural counties**</span>

<br/>

<span style="color:darkred">**Classroom: Under-funded rural schools; brain drain as students leave**</span>

<br/>

**This is painful....every one of us has likely a <span style="color:darkred">direct personal</span> relationship to at least one of these issues**

## Connect to the pain/problems/issues
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 45%;">

**Don’t bypass/avoid the uncomfortable**

<br/>

**It doesn’t need to be avoided or indulged but it needs to be acknowledged**

<br/>

**Even in college classes**

<br/>

<span style="color:blue">**By acknowledging it we can learn how to deal with it and how to make appropriate actions in the future to alter the root cause**</span>
</div>

## The underlying deep caring
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: right; width: 45%;">

<span style="color:blue">**Reinforce the truth:</span> that things wouldn’t be depressing if we didn’t care deeply**

<br/>

**<span style="color:darkred">Our caring is about the mountains and rivers we’d like future generations to inherit</span>**

<br/>

**Connecting to deep caring is totally different than a false “finding the silver lining”**

<br/>

**For example, this object in this picture could be reversed**
</div>

## The action that wants to emerge from the caring
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 48%;">

**Support actions that come organically from caring rather than guilt**

<br/>

**We agreed that we have an ethical and moral role to do something. However, we need to be careful on where the motivation comes from**

<br/>

**We now have constant real-time opportunities to practice this paradigm**

</div>

<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 99%;">

<br/>
<br/>

**<span style="color:darkred">In WV, people may have been led to believe the only choices were more extraction or no jobs. What if our caring points to different actions – like restoration jobs, heritage tourism, small-scale farming, community solar?</span>**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:220px; LEFT:550px; WIDTH:550px; HEIGHT:300px" SRC="images/external.png">
